summary: You have new medicines, two blood tests, an eye doctor referral, and a visit back in 3 months. You told us getting there and paying are hard. Here is a plan that uses the help we could check. Your first blood test (fasting) is due within 2 weeks, so start there.

steps.title: Get help paying for care and medicine
steps.action: Apply for Medicaid through Georgia Gateway, even if you are not sure you qualify or were turned down before. If you get care at Grady, also ask about the Grady Financial Assistance Program for discounted care.
steps.why: Coverage or a discount can lower the cost of your new metformin, your higher lisinopril dose, your blood tests, and your visits.

steps.title: Find a low-cost clinic close to you
steps.action: Mercy Care at Gateway Center is about 0.7 km away, near Garnett Station. Mercy Care Decatur Street is near King Memorial Station. These health centers charge on a sliding fee based on income. Ask them if they can help with your medicines, your blood tests, and your 3-month check-up.
steps.why: A nearby clinic with sliding fees can make your follow-up care cheaper and easier to reach by train.

steps.title: Get your fasting blood test in the next 2 weeks
steps.action: Your paper says go to any Quest or Labcorp lab. Do not eat before the test. Ask your clinic which lab is closest to a MARTA stop, and ask what the test will cost you before you go.
steps.why: This test checks your kidneys, which matters because of your medicines.

steps.title: Pay less for MARTA rides
steps.action: See if you qualify for a Reduced Fare Breeze Card. It is for seniors, people with disabilities, and Medicare cardholders. If you cannot ride regular buses or trains because of a disability, ask about MARTA Mobility (door-to-door paratransit).
steps.why: Cheaper or easier rides help you get to the lab, the eye doctor, and your next visit.

steps.title: Watch for the eye doctor's call
steps.action: Your paper says the eye doctor's office will call you to set up a diabetes eye check. If no one calls in 10 days, call the number on your paper. When they call, ask how to get there by MARTA and what it will cost.
steps.why: Diabetes can hurt your eyes, and this check catches problems early.

steps.title: Take your medicines the new way
steps.action: Start metformin 1 pill twice a day with meals. Take 2 lisinopril pills once a day now. Stop ibuprofen (Advil). Check your blood sugar each morning and write it down. Call the office if it is over 300 two times in a row. Call 911 for chest pain, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness on one side.
steps.why: These are the changes from your visit, and the warning signs to know.
